description:
Watch this video for a look at some of the recent standout games that have been developed by small and medium sized teams from around the world using Unreal Engine and the broader Epic ecosystem as rocket fuel to achieve big things.

This sizzle reel showcases the wide range of visual styles, gameplay experiences, and genres that can be created with Unreal Engine—from highly stylized worlds to photorealistic environments, and from cozy adventures to thrilling sci-fi combat.

To celebrate indie developer achievements and inspire what’s next, we invited a number of studios that embody the indie spirit to share their experiences and expertise in our Indie Games Week.

Check out exclusive indie interviews and Inside Unreal episodes packed with UE dev tips for small teams here: https://unrealengine.com/events/indie-games-week-2026

To find out more about building indie games with Unreal Engine, take a look at our website: unrealengine.com/uses/indie-games

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Watch this video and explore how Timberline’s 13-person indie team crafted ‘Beastro’, a crunchy cozy UE5-powered adventure that blends deckbuilding, cooking, and puppet-theater battles in a delicious game packed with bold visuals and quirky charm.

‘Beastro’ infuses elements from a variety of genres while bringing vibrant visuals, quirky characters, and engaging crafting mechanics to the forefront.

Drawn in by the art and animation tools of Unreal Engine 5, Timberline challenged itself to push the boundaries and produce the visually stunning puppet theater battles that serve as the “crunchier” side of the experience, while source code access and assistance from Epic’s community resources has helped the indie team achieve its goals.  

Get the full story in our interview with Timberline’s Game Director, Lindsey Rostal, Tech Director Bryan Pawlowski, and Technical Art Director/Animation Nathan Fulton: https://epic.gm/dev-interviews-beastro
